transcript: Last night I went to back to the future on Broadway. It's a very enjoyable production, a feast for the senses, really. I think it's the most impressive projections I've ever seen. First stage production, and there are honestly a lot of jaw dropping moments in terms of visual effects. I won't spoil the ending, but it is mind blowing. The cast is great, and there's a very funny chemistry between Casey Likes and Roger Bart as Marty and DOC. Overall, this musical stays pretty true to the movie, maintaining most of the iconic scenes and lines, and all the actors do a great job of embodying their characters. My only real critique was that the music was nothing special to me, and the placement of some of the songs felt a little forced. But in fairness, this is a hurdle that I feel like a lot of movie and musical adaptations struggle with. But the score was very well performed by everyone, especially Casey Likes and Jelani Remy, who plays Mayor Goldie Wilson. Back to the future is currently running at the Winter Garden Theatre. And now, as of last night, I visited all 40 one Broadway theatres. Lastly, tickets are a little pricey for this one, but the Winter Garden is not particularly deep, so I wouldn't say you have to splurge to avoid a bad seat because there really aren't any. I think this is gonna be a hit. With that, another playbill for my collection.
reasoning: Tyler gives a clear positive recommendation despite some music critiques. He calls it 'very enjoyable,' praises the impressive visuals and cast, and predicts it will be 'a hit,' indicating he'd recommend it to others.
